questions.question:
A Configuration Manager has configured a multiple data sources which are all authorized to update the same class and the same set of class attributes in the CMDB.
What can the Configuration Manager do to control which data source should be authoritative source of truth for a specific class of set of class attributes?
answers: A. Assign a priority to each data source in the reconciliation rules
B. Manually run the data source updates in the correct order
C. Configure data refresh rules with a specific time period
D. Assign a run order to each data source in the identification rules

comments.content:
When multiple authorized data sources update the same CI class and the same attributes, the Configuration Manager must control which source wins when conflicting values arrive.
That control lives in:

CMDB Reconciliation (Precedence) Rules
These rules allow you to:
**Set source‑level precedence (e.g., Discovery > SCCM > Import Set)
**Set attribute‑level precedence (e.g., SCCM wins for serial_number, Discovery wins for IP)
**Ensure all updates flow through IRE, preventing unauthorized overwrites
**Maintain a single authoritative source of truth per attribute
**This is the only mechanism designed for this purpose.

A. 
2 fields can be populated when creating the reconciliation rule: 
"discovery source"  & "priority"
A. Assign a priority to each data source in the reconciliation rules

questions.question:
Which CMDB 360/Multisource CMDB the Dynamic Reconciliation Rules will also be enabled. Based on the request of the management, a CMDB Administrator has to set up multiple Dynamic Reconciliation Rules.
Which are available ‘Dynamic Rule Types’ within the ‘Create Reconciliation Rule’ wizard? (Choose two.)

comments.content:
typical dynamic rules :

Most Reported
Last Updated

Dynamic reconciliation rules can be used to choose one of the following types of values from the Multisource CMDB data:

    First Reported
    Most Reported
    Last Reported
    Largest Value
    Smallest Value

Why these are correct
Dynamic Reconciliation Rules are used when you want the system to decide the authoritative value based on data behavior, not fixed precedence.
The available dynamic rule types are:
**Last Updated: The attribute value from the source with the most recent update timestamp wins.
**Most Reported: The attribute value that appears most frequently across all sources wins.
These are the only two dynamic rule types supported.

Why the others are incorrect
B. Smallest Value: Not a valid dynamic rule type. CMDB reconciliation never compares numeric magnitude.
C. Last Created: Creation timestamp is not used in reconciliation. Only update timestamp is relevant.
B. Smallest Value and D. Most Reported
Answer is B & D

questions.question:
The following identification rule for a CI class has been defined:

Two new CI records are imported into the hardware class of the CMDB:
CI1: The name of this CI record matches the name of an existing CI record in the CMDB.
CI2: The IP address of this CI record matches the IP address of an existing CI record in the CMDB.
Which is correct based on the identification rule and the imported CI records?
answers: A. CI1 will be inserted as new record and CI2 will be updated with matching record.
B. CI1 will be updated with matching record and CI2 will be inserted as new record.
C. CI1 and CI2 both will be updated with matching records.
D. CI1 and CI2 both will be inserted as new records.

comments.content:
How Identification Works for Hardware CIs
For the Hardware class, the Identification Rule typically evaluates attributes in this order:

Serial Number (highest priority)
Name
MAC Address
(Sometimes) IP address — but only if explicitly included in the Identification Rule

And here’s the critical part: If an attribute is NOT part of the Identification Rule, it is NOT used to match CIs.
Most Hardware identification rules do NOT use IP address as an identity key.

Apply this to the question
CI1: Name matches an existing CI
Name is part of the Identification Rule
**CI1 will match and update the existing CI

CI2: IP address matches an existing CI
IP address is NOT part of the Identification Rule
**CI2 will NOT match  
**CI2 will be inserted as a new CI
Answer is B

questions.question: What is the difference between Data Certification and Attestation policies when managing a CI?
answers: A. Attestation requires correcting specific attributes of a CI, while Data Certification tracks acknowledgement the CI still exists.
B. Attestation can be scheduled, while Data Certification cannot be scheduled.
C. Attestation tracks acknowledgement the CI still exists, while Data Certification requires validating specific attributes of a CI.
D. Attestation can be assigned to a Group or an individual, while Data Certification can only be assigned to an individual.

comments.content:
Why this is the correct distinction
Attestation
Asks: “Does this CI still exist in the environment?”
**A simple yes/no acknowledgement
**Used to confirm existence, ownership, or responsibility
**Does not require checking individual attributes
Think of it as:“Is this server still real and in use?”

Data Certification
Asks: “Are the attributes of this CI accurate and up to date?”
**Requires reviewing and validating specific fields

questions.question: Which are CMDB Data Manager end of life policy types? (Choose two.)

comments.content:
Types of Data Manager Policies
ServiceNow provides three primary types of Data Manager Policies:

Retire Policies – Mark CIs as retired when they are no longer in use but need to be retained for historical reference. These policies help organizations track assets that are phased out without cluttering active operational data.
Archive Policies – Move records to an archive table when they are no longer actively needed but should be kept for compliance. Archiving helps maintain a balance between accessibility and performance optimization.
Delete Policies – Permanently remove records that are no longer required, freeing up system resources. These policies help organizations enforce data retention strategies while keeping the CMDB lean.
archive retire
Only A and B
The primary policy types are Retire, Archive, and Delete, which automate the handling of stale or outdated CIs, supported by specialized policies for related items
